Identify the nearest neighbor: Calculate the Euclidean distance between the novel view position $\mathbf{p}_{novel}$ and every training view position $\mathbf{p}_i$.
Retrieve the exposure setting (or implicit exposure scaling factor) associated with $I_{nn}$.
Apply the exposure correction from $I_{nn}$ to the rendered radiance at $V_{novel}$.
Calculate the averaged color $(r_a, g_a, b_a) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ of all input images in the set $S$.
Select a reference image $I_{ref}$ which has the closest averaged color value $(r_{ref}, g_{ref}, b_{ref}) \in \mathbb{R}^3$ to $(r_a, g_a, b_a)$.
Fix the white balance of this reference image as regularization.
Estimate the reference color ratio by comparing per-image averaged pixel values to the averaging of each RGB value from the entire image set $S$.
*   **Time Complexity:** The nearest-neighbor search is $O(N)$ per novel view, where $N$ is the number of training views.
